summary.one_liner: chardet is a Python library and CLI that detects the character encoding of raw byte data, rewritten from the ground up as version 7 under the 0BSD license.
summary.what_it_does: Detects the character encoding of byte strings via detect(), detect_all() (ranked candidates with confidence), and UniversalDetector for incremental streaming input. Returns encoding, confidence, detected language, and MIME type for binary files (40+ formats via magic numbers, plus text/html, text/xml, text/x-python). Supports encoding era filtering and include/exclude encoding lists. Ships a chardetect CLI with options for minimal output, language, and encoding restriction, and reads from stdin. The README states 99 supported Python codecs with 86 detection targets, and 99.7% accuracy on a 3,138-file test set.
use_cases: detect the encoding of an unknown text file
identify charset of web or network byte streams
batch-check legacy files for encoding before conversion
filter encoding guesses to a known set of code pages
identify file MIME type from magic bytes
command-line encoding checks in shell pipelines
notable: Drop-in replacement API for chardet 5.x and 6.x, rewritten from scratch under 0BSD license
Language detection returned with every result, plus MIME type detection for binary files
Encoding era filtering (e.g. MODERN_WEB, MAINFRAME) to reduce false positives
Streaming detection via UniversalDetector and a thread-safe detect() call
Optional compiled builds claiming about 4.5x extra speedup on CPython
caveats: Optional compiled speedups apply to CPython builds; the 3,125 files/s figure is for the compiled version (771 pure)
Performance and accuracy figures are the author's benchmarks; the README does not describe the test corpus beyond the file count
Versions 5.x and 6.x are LGPL and use separate code, per the README history section
